CUSTOMS NOTIFICATION
Customs Ordinance (Chapter 235)

IN pursuance of the power vested in me by the Section 103B(1) of the Customs Ordinance (Chapter 235), I, RaviKarunanayake, Minister of Finance, do hereby promulgated these regulations for issuance of Non Manipulation Certificateeffective from the date of publication of these regulation in the Government Gazette.
RAVI KARUNANAYAKE,Minister of Finance.
Ministry of Finance,Colombo 01,01st January 2016.
REGULATIONS
These regulations may be cited as the “Non Manipulation Certificate Regulations” and shall come into operation on thedate these Regulations are published in the Government Gazette.

1. The Director General of Customs is hereby empowered to issue, on the request of a Master of every ship orby a ship’s agent with the express or implied consent of such Master hereinafter called as the ‘Carrier’, a“Non-Manipulation Certificate” in respect of “Non-Manipulated Cargo”
2. Non-Manipulated Cargo”
For the purpose of these Regulations, Non-Manipulated Cargo shall mean consignments that fulfill all of thefollowing conditions :-

(a) The consignment shall be containerized cargo sent from beyond the territorial limits of Sri Lanka,destined for another country via the Airports or Sea Ports of Sri Lanka, after having been transshippedin Sri Lanka.

(b) The container arrived in Sri Lanka under a tamperproof seal placed by the carrier and the said sealremained intact until the container was loaded onboard the vessel, or the aircraft, in a Sri Lankan Portfor its final departure from Sri Lanka.
(c) From the time of arrival in Sri Lanka up to the time of loading onboard for final depature, the containerremained under the supervision and control of Sri Lanka Customs.

(d) Throughout the period the container remained in Sri Lanka, its contents were not altered in any manner,and the container was not subjected to any operations other than those required to preserve its contentsin good condition.

3. On arrival of the containers, the carrier’s designated local agent who intends to obtain a “Non-ManipulationCertificate” shall communicate this to the Director General of Customs, who shall thereupon make availablethe services of Customs Supervision. Thereafter, after the container has been transshipped for final departure,he shall make a request for a Non-Manipulation Certificate with regard to the cargo transshipped via SriLanka and fulfilling the requirements of paragraph (2) of these Regulations.

4. The Carrier’s designated local agent applying for the Non-Manipulation Certificate shall also certify in thesame application that the container/s, for which a Non-Manipulation Certificate was requested, had fulfilledall the conditions specified in paragraph (2) of these Regulations.

5. Thereupon, if the Director General of Customs is satisfied that the conditions stipulated under paragraph (2)of these regulations have been fulfilled, he shall issue a Non-Manipulation Certificate in the format as depictedin the annex hereto, on recovery of the fee prescribed in paragraph (6) of these Regulations.

6. The Director General of Customs shall charge a fee for each certificate so issued ; which fee shall initially bean amount equivalent to US$ 10/- per certificate. The said fee will be periodically revised in consultationwith the Minister in charge of Finance.
